To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the metal-metal interaction in the dinuclear cationic Pt(II) complex is not supported by any ligands and thus represents an unprecedented example of unsupported metal-metal bonding in a Pt(II) system, and 2) a similar unsupported d8-d8 interaction in the dinuclar cationic PdBis(terpy)2 complex has been established by theoretical calculations.

the d(8)- d(8) interactions in these complexes are not supported by bridging ligands, and that these interactions exhibit significant metal-metal bonding characteristics for both Pd(II)-Pd(II) systems and Pt(II)-Pt(II) systems.
we have synthesized two new isoelectronic dinuclear Pd(II)- and Pt(II)-containing complexes that display unsupported d(8)- d(8) interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel transition metal complexes with a focus on the development of new synthetic strategies and applications of these complexes in organic synthesis.
the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of transition metal complexes.
the synthesis, characterization and reactivity of new metal-metal bonded complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pd-Pd and Pt-Pt interactions in these systems are supported by a combination of electrostatic, d-d orbital, d-d overlap, and metal-metal bonding interactions.
the Pd-Pd and Pt-Pt distances in these complexes are too close for a purely electrostatic attraction and that there is a significant metal-metal interaction in the dicationic complexes.
the metal-metal interaction in the Pd(II)-Pd(II) complex is not supported by a bridging ligand, and thus, it is not a simple dative interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the metal-metal interaction in these complexes is a significant bonding interaction, and not just an electrostatic attraction between the two metal centers.
the d(8)- d(8) interactions in these complexes are not only supported by a single bridging ligand, but also by two bridging ligands, and now, by no bridging ligands.
we have shown the first examples of unsupported d(8)- d(8) interactions in Pd(II), and that these interactions are not limited to Pd(II).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pd-Pd and Pt-Pt distances of 3.3 and 3.2 angstroms, respectively, are significantly shorter than the sum of the van der Waals radii of the metals.
d8-d8 interactions in cation complexes can be significant and can lead to the stabilization of the cationic complexes in solution and in the solid state.
metal-metal interactions in cationically coordinated metal complexes are not only possible but also significant.
